sophia: Just uploaded a perfetto trace for the e2e request that showed a weird latency spike around 110-140ms. Trace: https://perfetto.google/chrome/trace#trace=abc123def456 :eyes:
perf-bot: Upload complete — trace ID abc123def456 (size 28MB)

maria: jumping in — saw it. Kernel timeline shows a 20ms sequence of cuMemcpyAsync and a long kernel launch gap around 118ms.

jamal: can you paste the top-level waterfall? I want to see client->gateway->runtime spans alignment.

sophia: here's the condensed waterfall from perfetto (snip):
```
client request 0.0 - 6.2ms
gateway enqueue 6.2 - 9.8ms
gateway dispatch 9.8 - 12.0ms
runtime prepare 12.0 - 14.0ms
runtime kv-lookup 14.0 - 116.5ms  <-- long
runtime kernel exec 116.5 - 138.4ms
runtime memcpy 138.4 - 140.0ms
```

kai: runtime kv-lookup for 1024-token inputs shouldn't be 100ms. Is KV cache doing a blocking fetch from host? May be spilling to CPU memory.

maria: +1. I see repeated small reads in the trace before 116ms — cache miss storm maybe. Check httprouter/gateway logs for request batching around that time.

jamal: I ran nsys on a repro run earlier. nvtx shows repeated host->device memcpy scatter followed by cudaLaunchKernel gaps. Could be our kernel selection picking an unfused attention kernel for this sequence length.

sophia: command I used to capture: `perfetto --txt -o /tmp/trace.pbz2 --config perf_cfg.pbtxt` and nsys capture: `nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys -t cuda,cuda_api,osrt --sample=cpu ./run_infer`

kai: kernel selection hypothesis: our selector uses heuristic: if seq_len > 512 pick kernel B; maybe a boundary bug at 512->513. This trace is 520 tokens. If selector falls back to generic kernel that serializes warps, launch overhead rises.

maria: can we correlate kernel names in perfetto with our kernel table? Look at kernel name column; I see `attn_forward_v2` and a later `attn_fallback_generic` around the spike.

jamal: yeah that confirms fallback. Also note the memcpy burst right before fallback — likely syncing async streams to move KV chunks. That synchronization is causing the 20ms stall.

sophia: quick repro idea: run same request with KV cache warm vs cold and measure gateway->runtime latency. If cold is bad we have eviction/restore issue.

kai: ok I'll run a 100-req batch with kv_warm=true/false and upload traces. Will also run `nvprof --analysis-metrics ...` to check achieved occupancy for both kernels.
